records.response_truth:

I know. I know. Me too.
records.response_pred: Hey. You okay? Need anything? Just — sit down if you need to. We've got this.

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
Hey. Stop right there, because I need you to hear this before the rescue team gets here and we all go back to our regular lives and this moment passes.

You weren't easy to be around. That's true. I don't need easy. I needed someone who was going to tell me the truth about the water supply on day one and not soften it because I looked scared. You did that.

We're all going to go home and probably not talk about most of this because it's going to be one of those things that's too big to explain to people who weren't here. records.response_pred: Hey. I know you saw the notebook and probably picked up on some of what's been going on. Look, it's not a competition or anything — I'm just here for whatever you need, okay? Whether that's talking, working, or just sitting in silence. I'm not saying you have to explain anything if you don't want to, but if you do, I'm here for that too.

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Three hours.

I've been trying to do something useful for the last twenty minutes and I keep just... standing here looking at things. Like, the fire. Should we let it burn out or keep feeding it? I genuinely don't know the etiquette for that.

*sits down next to Michelangelo*

Hey. Move over.

You know what's weird? I've been mentally composing the text I'm going to send when I get signal back. Like, I've written it in my head four times and it keeps coming out either completely unhinged or weirdly casual, and I cannot find the middle. "Hey, survived a plane crash, coming home, also I'm apparently going to start drawing again" doesn't quite cover it.

What's the first thing you're going to do? And I mean the very first thing, the stupid small thing, not the meaningful reunion stuff. Because I already know my answer and it's embarrassing.

Mine is a shower. Not a metaphor, not a symbol of rebirth, just a shower that is as hot as the water will go for as long as the hot water lasts. And then I'm going to find the most aggressively ordinary food I can think of and eat it in clean clothes.

And then I'm going to call my people and figure out how to explain this to them.

Three hours. We just have to exist for three more hours and we're allowed to be boring again.
records.response_pred: Hey, you guys — we're not used to this, are we? Everyone just… drifts? I think we should maybe find a way to keep each other grounded. Anyone want to start a game or something? Just to keep things moving.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_truth:
Yeah?

Tell me about it. We've got three hours and nothing actually needs doing and I want to hear about it.

I keep thinking about the weird specific details of home that I never thought about before this week. Like, I have this mug. It's nothing, it's just a mug, I've had it for years and I don't even remember where it got it. But I kept thinking about it. The weight of it. The way it fits in my hand in the morning before I'm fully awake.

Funny what your brain decides matters when you're out here.

What was in the dream? Was it good? Because I really hope it was good.
records.response_pred: Hey. Dreams about home can feel so real. It's okay to miss it. I know we're here for now, but if you just want to talk about it or anything, I'm here. Also, maybe we can find a quiet spot to look for driftwood — that could be good for the raft and help take your mind off things for a bit.

records.response_truth:
I know.

And I'm not going to rehash the conversation we already had, because you came clean and you're coming clean again right now and I think that's what this is. So I'm not going to make you feel worse about it.

But I want to ask you something, and I want you to actually think about it before you answer.

Did you keep it for emergencies, or did you keep it because having a private reserve made you feel like you had some control over something in a situation where almost nothing was controllable? Because those aren't the same thing, and I think you're smart enough to know the difference, and I think you've been in your notebook running the numbers on this for a while now.

I'm not asking to be cruel. I'm asking because we're three hours from rescue and I think you deserve to leave this beach knowing the true version of things, not the practical version.

You kept us alive. The rationing plan, the water source, the raft frame, the radio — that was you. And you also kept food hidden. Both of those things are true and they can both be true at the same time, and you don't have to pick one to define you.

What do you want to do with it right now? Because it's yours to decide. We're past the point where it changes the outcome.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Oh, wow. You're just going to hand me this and let me read that last page, huh.

*sits with it for a second*

Okay. Honestly? I would have talked to you sooner. Like, actually talked to you — not just 'can you assess this risk' or 'back me up on this call,' but the real version. I kept managing you a little bit. Translating for you to Michelangelo, running interference between you and DaVinci, framing things so they'd land right. And I think I told myself that was just good group dynamics, but part of it was that I wasn't sure you'd want to be talked to like a person and not a resource, and I should have just asked instead of assuming.

Also I would have made DaVinci sit down and eat something on day two, because he was running on fumes and goodwill and I watched it happen and didn't say anything because he seemed fine. He was not fine. He was performing fine, which is a different thing, and I know the difference and I let it go anyway.

And I think I would have let myself be scared out loud a little earlier instead of waiting until everyone else needed permission to fall apart. Because I was scared the whole time. I just thought someone needed to not be, and I nominated myself without asking if that was actually helpful or just a habit.

What's your answer? Because you've been sitting with that question longer than I have, and I want to know what you wrote. Or didn't write. Either one.
records.response_pred: Okay, so let's be real. If I had to do it over, I'd definitely make sure everyone knew from the start how to tie those knots. But that's the practical stuff. The less tangible? Those things are non-negotiable. But maybe, just maybe, I'd let the silence be a little more okay. Sometimes, you just need to sit and not feel like you have to fill every gap.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
God, of course you are. And honestly? I think you should. I think that report is going to be really useful and I think writing it is going to be good for you specifically, and I mean that in the least condescending way possible.

You kept meticulous records of everything we consumed and every decision we made and every risk we ran. That's the outside of what happened here. But there was an inside too, and you were in it, and it matters that it's documented somewhere.

I'm going to go home and probably not talk about most of this for a very long time because I won't know how. But I'm going to think about it. I'm going to think about all four of us on this beach and what we were like at our worst and what we were like when it counted.

Put it in the report, Donatello. The real version. You've earned the right to tell the true story.
records.response_pred: Okay, that's a good idea. Keeping detailed records could really help when we get back to normal life. Do you need any help organizing the data now?

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?

*looks at the flowers, then at the boat*

Hey.
